origin: hand-written from the published schema; every value invented
notes: A management key cannot call the completion endpoints, so its usage counters stay at zero and it carries no credit cap. is_management_key is the cheapest honest way to learn the presented key's permission category WITHOUT probing the balance - architecture forbids using inference calls to test authentication - but the field is only documented in the API reference example, so its presence is unverified and no code may depend on it yet. expires_at matters operationally: expiry is fixed at creation and cannot be extended, and an expired key makes every request fail 401 'API key expired', so rotation has to be scheduled ahead of it. A management key is account-scoped and unscoped across workspaces, and the same credential also unlocks destructive key, BYOK and guardrail routes - which is why the read-only allow-list has to be enforced in code.
